q.t: How many degrees are there at the centre of a full circle?
q.e: One complete turn is 360°, and a pie chart shares this out.

q.t: The whole pie chart stands for what percent?
q.e: The full circle is the whole — all 100%.

q.t: What central angle shows 25% in a pie chart (in degrees)?
What central angle shows one half (in degrees)?
A pie chart is used to show:
o: How a whole is divided into parts
q.e: Each sector’s size shows that part’s share of the whole.

q.t: What central angle shows 1/3 (in degrees)?
What central angle shows 10% (in degrees)?
A sector has a central angle of 90°. What fraction of the whole is it?
A sector has a central angle of 72°. What percent of the whole is it?
All the central angles of a pie chart add up to:
q.e: Together the sectors fill the whole circle.

q.t: 60 students out of 240 walk to school. What is the central angle for them (in degrees)?
From a monthly budget of ₹12,000, ₹3000 goes on rent. What is the central angle for rent (in degrees)?
A sector has a central angle of 54°. What percent does it show?
What central angle shows 35% (in degrees)?
A sector of 150° is drawn in a pie chart whose total is 720. How many does the sector stand for?
A pie chart has three sectors. Two of them are 120° and 150°. Find the third (in degrees).
In a survey of 500 students, the football sector is 40% of the pie. How many chose football?
What central angle shows 5/12 of the whole (in degrees)?
A sector has a central angle of 45°. What fraction is it?
A sector of 60° stands for 90 students. How many students does the whole pie chart show?
q.e: 60° is one sixth of the circle, so the total is 6 × 90 = 540.

q.t: A pie chart shows A 30%, B 25%, C 20% and D the rest. Find the central angle for D (in degrees).
In a family’s pie chart the food sector is 108° and monthly income is ₹20,000. How much is spent on food (in ₹)?
Food is 108° and rent is 72° in a pie chart of a ₹20,000 income. How much more is spent on food than on rent (in ₹)?
q.e: The 36° difference is one tenth of the circle: 2000.

q.t: The savings sector of 54° stands for ₹4500. Find the total income (in ₹).
5400 votes are shown in a pie chart. The winner’s sector is 144° and the runner-up’s is 96°. By how many votes did the winner win?
Three sectors of a pie chart are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest central angle (in degrees).
q.e: 9 parts make 360°, one part is 40°, largest = 160°.

q.t: 18 students make up 10% of a pie chart. How many students does the whole chart show?
45 out of 300 students cycle to school. Find the central angle for them (in degrees).
A sector of 100° stands for 250 people. How many does a sector of 36° stand for?
A sector has a central angle of 81°. What percent does it show?
A pie chart of a student’s 540 marks has Hindi 100°, English 80°, Maths 90° and Science the rest. Find the marks in Hindi.
In the same chart (540 marks: Hindi 100°, English 80°, Maths 90°, Science the rest), how many more marks are there in Maths than in English?
In the same chart (Hindi 100°, English 80°, Maths 90°, Science the rest), what percent of the marks came from Science?
q.e: Science = 360 − 270 = 90°, a quarter of the circle.

q.t: The four sectors of a pie chart have angles a, 2a, 3a and 4a. What percent is the largest sector?
q.e: The parts are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4, so the largest is 4/10 = 40%.

q.t: Four of the five sectors of a pie chart are 72°, 54°, 90° and 108°. What percent is the fifth?
A family spends 20% on rent, 30% on food, 35% on other things and saves the rest, which is ₹6000. Find its income (in ₹).
A family spends 20% on rent, 30% on food, 35% on other things and saves the rest. What is the central angle for savings (in degrees)?
School A has 400 students with a 90° cricket sector. School B has 600 students with a 72° cricket sector. How many more students play cricket in B than in A?
q.e: A: 1/4 of 400 = 100. B: 1/5 of 600 = 120. A bigger angle does not mean more students when the totals differ.

q.t: What central angle shows 37.5% (in degrees)?
The three sectors of a pie chart are (2x + 10)°, 3x° and (4x − 10)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 9x = 360, so x = 40. The angles are 90°, 120° and 150°.
